web.title: Mithai Pehchano: Blindfold Sweet Tasting Kitty Party Game
web.description: Mithai Pehchano is a blindfold sweet tasting game for kitty parties. Learn how to play, what you need, the rules, fun twists and tips for Diwali.
web.intro: Mithai Pehchano is a blindfold tasting game where each lady tastes one small piece of Indian mithai and has 10 seconds to name it. Every correct name scores a point, and the lady with the most points at the end wins. The twist: anyone who guesses wrong has to bring that exact mithai to the next kitty. It is perfect for Diwali week, needs only leftover sweets, a dupatta and toothpicks, and takes about 15 minutes.
materials: 5 to 6 kinds of mithai (kaju katli, laddoo, barfi, peda, soan papdi), cut into one-bite pieces
A dupatta or scarf as a blindfold
Toothpicks, a fresh one for each lady
Paper and pen to keep score
steps: Cut 5 to 6 kinds of mithai into small one-bite pieces and keep them on a plate, out of sight of the players.
Blindfold one lady with a dupatta. Everyone else stays quiet and gives no hints.
The host picks a piece with a fresh toothpick and feeds it to the blindfolded lady.
Start a 10 second timer. If she names the mithai correctly, she gets 1 point.
If she names it wrong, she must bring that exact mithai to the next kitty. Repeat for every lady, 2 or 3 rounds each.
rules: Peeking from under the blindfold cancels the point.
An answer after 10 seconds does not count.
Anyone who gives a hint loses one of her own points.
The lady with the most correct answers is the Mithai Queen.
variations: Feed two pieces at once and ask for both names.
Ask for the city as well, like Agra ka petha or Mathura ka peda.
Give only 5 seconds in the final round.
tips: Ask about nut allergies, diabetes or fasting before you start, and keep a sugar free option ready.
Use a fresh toothpick for every lady.
Cut pieces really small so nothing is wasted; leftovers go back in the box for tea time.
Keep one tricky pair, like barfi and milk cake, to make it harder.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Mithai Pehchano?
faq.a: It works for 8 to 20 ladies. Each lady takes her turn alone, so bigger groups simply play fewer rounds each.

faq.q: What do you need to play the blindfold mithai game?
faq.a: 5 to 6 kinds of mithai cut into bite size pieces, a dupatta as a blindfold, toothpicks, a phone timer and a paper to keep score.

faq.q: Is Mithai Pehchano a good Diwali kitty party game?
faq.a: Yes. It uses the sweets that are already in every home during Diwali, needs no setup and gets everyone laughing at the wrong guesses.

faq.q: Which sweets are best for a mithai tasting game?
faq.a: Mix easy and tricky ones: kaju katli, motichoor laddoo, peda, soan papdi, plain barfi, milk cake or coconut barfi. Similar looking sweets make it harder.

faq.q: What if someone has diabetes or a nut allergy?
faq.a: Ask before the game. Keep sugar free sweets or nut free options for her, or let her play as the host who feeds and times the others.
